edges.description: Infiltrating macrophages secrete proteolytic enzymes that degrade the aortic extracellular matrix.
MMP activity degrades the elastin and fibrillar collagen that provide aortic wall strength.
edges.target: Elastin and collagen extracellular matrix degradation

edges.description: Loss of structural matrix accompanies and promotes depletion of medial smooth muscle cells.
edges.source: Elastin and collagen extracellular matrix degradation
edges.target: Medial smooth muscle cell depletion and wall thinning

edges.description: A weakened, thinned wall dilates progressively and is at risk of rupture.
edges.source: Medial smooth muscle cell depletion and wall thinning

nodes.description: Chronic transmural inflammation of the aortic wall, with infiltration of macrophages and lymphocytes, is an early and sustained feature of AAA. The inflammatory infiltrate drives local production of proteolytic enzymes and pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., IL-6) that promote extracellular matrix breakdown and aneurysm progression.

evidence.reference_title: The contribution of matrix metalloproteinases and their inhibitors to the development, progression, and rupture of abdominal aortic aneurysms.
evidence.snippet: Pathological observations advocate inflammatory cell infiltration alongside adverse extracellular matrix degradation as key contributing factors to the formation of human atherosclerotic AAAs.

evidence.reference_title: The Association of Biomarkers of Inflammation and Extracellular Matrix Degradation With the Risk of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: The ARIC Study.
evidence.snippet: blood concentrations of MMP-9 and IL-6 measured in middle age predicted the risk of AAA during 24 years of follow-up.

nodes.description: Proteolytic loss of medial elastic lamellae and fibrillar collagen removes the principal load-bearing components of the aortic wall. Elastin fragmentation reduces recoil and compliance, while collagen degradation ultimately compromises tensile strength and predisposes to rupture.
nodes.id: Elastin and collagen extracellular matrix degradation

evidence.snippet: AAA results from changes in the aortic wall structure, including thinning of the media and adventitia due to the loss of vascular smooth muscle cells and degradation of the extracellular matrix.

nodes.description: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is an investigational agent shown in a rat AAA model and network-pharmacology analysis to reduce MMP-2/MMP-9-mediated extracellular matrix degradation via inhibition of GABA-A-receptor-dependent PI3K/AKT signaling, delaying aneurysm progression. Preclinical only; no established human role.

evidence.reference_title: Exploring the potential mechanism of GABA in the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm through network pharmacology and experimental validation.
evidence.snippet: GABA reduced the expression and activity of MMP2 and MMP9, thereby effectively inhibiting ECM degradation and delaying the progression of AAA.

evidence.reference_title: Exploring the potential mechanism of GABA in the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm through network pharmacology and experimental validation.
evidence.snippet: KEGG analysis showed that the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway was the key pathway through which GABA exerted its therapeutic effects.

nodes.description: Macrophage- and smooth muscle cell-derived matrix metalloproteinases (notably MMP-2 and MMP-9) are the predominant proteinases in the AAA wall. A shift in the balance between MMPs and their tissue inhibitors (TIMPs) toward net proteolysis drives destruction of the load-bearing matrix. MMP-9 is elevated in the circulation of patients who later develop AAA.

evidence.reference_title: The contribution of matrix metalloproteinases and their inhibitors to the development, progression, and rupture of abdominal aortic aneurysms.
evidence.snippet: macrophage production of proteolytic enzymes is deemed responsible for the damaging loss of ECM proteins, especially elastin and fibrillar collagens, which characterise AAA progression and rupture.

evidence.reference_title: The Association of Biomarkers of Inflammation and Extracellular Matrix Degradation With the Risk of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: The ARIC Study.
evidence.snippet: Higher concentrations of MMP-9 and IL-6 were associated with future risk of clinically diagnosed AAA

nodes.description: Apoptosis and loss of medial vascular smooth muscle cells, the cells that synthesize and maintain the aortic matrix, thins the media and adventitia and impairs the wall's capacity to repair ongoing matrix injury.
nodes.id: Medial smooth muscle cell depletion and wall thinning

evidence.snippet: thinning of the media and adventitia due to the loss of vascular smooth muscle cells

nodes.description: Cumulative loss of wall strength allows progressive dilatation of the infrarenal aorta. Rupture occurs when the mechanical wall stress imposed by arterial blood pressure exceeds the residual wall strength; rupture risk rises with aneurysm diameter and carries very high mortality.

evidence.snippet: If the mechanical stress of the blood pressure acting on the wall exceeds the wall strength, the AAA ruptures, causing life-threatening intra-abdominal haemorrhage - the mortality for patients with ruptured AAA is 65-85%.
Although AAAs of any size can rupture, the risk of rupture increases with diameter.
